title: Tests for functional groups
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-02T04:41:50Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: The bank card covers the bromine water test for C=C and the sodium carbonate test for carboxylic acids, but it has no test for the hydroxyl group, so it is narrower than the new point and would need a new step to fit.

draft.title: Tests for functional groups
card: C=C double bond
Add bromine water, which is orange-brown. An alkene decolourises it quickly, because bromine adds across the double bond. A saturated compound does not decolourise it quickly in the dark.
Hydroxyl group
An alcohol has an -OH group. Warm it with acidified potassium dichromate, which is orange. A primary or secondary alcohol turns the mixture green, as the dichromate is reduced to chromium(III) ions.
Carboxyl group
A carboxylic acid has a -COOH group. Add sodium carbonate or sodium hydrogencarbonate. A carboxylic acid fizzes, because carbon dioxide gas forms.
Each test gives one visible change, such as a colour change or bubbles. The change points to one functional group.
draft.remember: Match the change to the group: bromine water goes colourless for C=C, dichromate goes green for an alcohol, and fizzing shows a carboxylic acid.

a.q: A colourless liquid is added to sodium carbonate powder and fizzes. Which functional group does it contain?
opts: Carboxyl group
Hydroxyl group
Carbon-carbon double bond
Carbon-carbon single bond only
a.why: Fizzing with a carbonate means carbon dioxide formed, which shows an acid with a carboxyl group. A hydroxyl group is tested with dichromate, which gives a colour change, not bubbles.
a.clue: Which group makes a carbonate release gas?

b.q: Priya tests a sample of unknown liquid X. It stays orange-brown with bromine water, but warmed acidified dichromate turns green. What does X most likely contain?
opts: A hydroxyl group but no C=C double bond
A C=C double bond but no hydroxyl group
Both a hydroxyl group and a C=C double bond
A carboxyl group and no hydroxyl group
b.why: Bromine water was not decolourised, so there is no C=C bond. Dichromate turning green shows an alcohol with a hydroxyl group. A carboxyl group would not be shown by the dichromate test.
b.clue: Read each test result separately, then combine them.

b.best: A hydroxyl group but no C=C double bond

problems.detail: 'The change points to one functional group' overstates it. Aldehydes also turn acidified dichromate green, and VCE students meet aldehydes as oxidation products of primary alcohols. Tertiary alcohols have an -OH group but give no change. Better wording: the change 'suggests' the group, with the main exceptions noted.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations match the card. One minor issue: the card says each test's change points to only one functional group, but aldehydes also turn dichromate green, so that line should be softened.
